messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1834 — elevated 5xx rate and latency spike on /v1/generate (us-west-2). Paging on-call: maya (SRE). auto-detection: sudden drop in prefix cache hit-rate.

maya (SRE): Paging in. seeing 4xx/5xx from runner pool, but initial traces show increased origin latency from runtime when KV lookups miss. attaching quick hit-rate snapshot.

emily (prod-analytics): sending timeline:
```
09:02:00 - baseline prefix hit-rate ~92%
09:05:20 - hit-rate drops to 64%
09:06:00 - bulk of errors start (~20rps 5xx)
09:10:00 - hit-rate bottoms at 38%
09:20:00 - partial recovery to 75% after mitigation
```

kevin (eng-runtime): copying logs from runtime (filtered):
```
[09:06:01] runner-12 kv-lookup key=prefix:abcd123 -> MISS (TTL expired)
[09:06:01] runner-12 fallback fetch backend_latency=185ms
[09:06:02] runner-07 kv-invalidate prefix:abcd123 triggered by invalidation-service (req id: inv-9f3)
[09:06:03] runner-03 alloc waiting for CPU, queue_len=23
```
We also see a flurry of invalidation events around 09:06.

sanjay (eng-sre): FYI we rolled a policy change earlier today (08:50) that lowered default prefix TTL from 6h -> 2h for one shard to reduce staleness. Could that be related?

lex (customer-sre): Customer impact: multiple customers in PLG tier reported short lived failures in chat attempts, roughly 1-2 minute window of errors, then retries succeeded. No billing anomalies reported yet.

maya (SRE): Hypothesis list: 1) Aggressive TTL change led to mass invalidations causing cold cache amplification + backend pressure. 2) Invalidation-service produced duplicate invalidation messages (retry bug) — causing repeated evictions. 3) KV node GC/compaction coincided causing transient increased miss latency.

kevin (eng-runtime): I can reproduce locally-ish: run with synthetic traffic that simulates prefix churn — cache warms but invalidations came in bursts, KV clients open many simultaneous fetches leading to queueing. Short-term mitigation options: a) throttle invalidation events, b) increase TTL back to previous value, c) enable local per-runner soft-stale/serve-stale policy to avoid sync fetch.

maya (SRE): Immediate mitigation executed:
- increased per-prefix soft-serve window from 0s -> 30s (keeps returning slightly stale cached entries while backend fetch in progress)
- rate-limited invalidation-service to 50 req/s per-shard
- scaled up KV read pool by 30% (temp)
Result: error rate dropped by 80% within 3 minutes, hit-rate recovered to ~70% in 8 minutes.

ops-bot: deploy event: config change 'soft-serve-window=30s' applied to runtime fleet at 09:13 by maya.

emily (prod-analytics): quick customer impact summary: ~320 failed requests during window across 12 customers. Median latency for affected requests increased from 120ms -> 620ms.

kevin (eng-runtime): attaching a short log excerpt where we saw duplicate invalidations within 2s:
```
09:05:59 invalidation-service shard-4 publish prefix:abcd123 id=inv-9f3
09:06:00 invalidation-service shard-4 publish prefix:abcd123 id=inv-9f3 (retry)
09:06:00 invalidation-service shard-4 publish prefix:abcd123 id=inv-9f3 (duplicate)
```
This looks like at-least-once delivery + no de-dupe key on subscriber side.

sanjay (eng-sre): I'll open a quick mitigation PR to add idempotency check on subscriber and a short de-dupe window. But that's mid-term. For next 24h, recommend reverting TTL change that went live at 08:50 to avoid repeated cold starts.

maya (SRE): Agreed. Can someone from runtime do the TTL revert? It's config push to config-service, non-disruptive.

kevin (eng-runtime): On it. Planning a config rollback to 6h TTL. Will push to staging, then prod staging group first, then full. ETA 15m.

lex (customer-sre): I'll draft a short customer note: impacted customers saw transient request failures between 09:06-09:12, now resolved; will follow up with RCA.

emily (prod-analytics): adding a chart link (prod dashboard): https://dash.redwood.internal/incident/1834/hitrate which shows per-shard lines — shard-4 is the outlier.

maya (SRE): Handoff plan: kevin -> sanjay for postmortem. If issues recur during rollback, page maya. Document artifacts to collect: full invalidation-service audit logs, KV node metrics (latency, compaction events), runtime per-runner queue lengths, and the config diff for TTL change.

kevin (eng-runtime): rollback to 6h TTL scheduled: initiating now.

ops-bot: config-change: ttl.default_prefix set to "6h" by kevin at 09:22. rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% (completed 09:29).

maya (SRE): After rollback, observed: no further error spikes; hit-rate climbing back to 88% by 09:33.

emily (prod-analytics): final numbers:
- total failed requests: 324
- peak errors/sec: 18 at 09:07
- customers impacted: 12, highest per-customer error count = 97
- time-to-mitigation (soft-serve + rate-limit): 7m

kevin (eng-runtime): Next actions (short):
- add de-dupe on invalidation subscription (PR queued)
- add metrics/alert for invalidation-burst (>20 invalidations/shard/min)
- review config rollout gating for TTL changes (don't allow global drop from 6h->2h without staged ramp)

sanjay (eng-sre): I'll own the postmortem write-up and include timeline, logs, and proposed fixes. Will include a short appendix showing KV compaction metrics (no compaction coincident here). Also will coordinate follow-up with invalidation-service team.

lex (customer-sre): Customer comms draft ready, will send after PM review.

maya (SRE): Closing on-call note: stabilize and handoff to sanjay. If anything flares, page "maya (SRE)".

sanjay (eng-sre): Taking post-incident owner. I'll create the incident doc and link artifacts to the ticket.

incident-bot: Incident 1834 status -> mitigated. Severity: Sev3.

maya (SRE): Thanks all. Quick retrospective point: config safety for cache parameters needs stronger staging and synthetic churn tests.

kevin (eng-runtime): Agreed. I'll add a sim that replays invalidation bursts against the local cache impl to catch amplification.

sanjay (eng-sre): ETA for postmortem draft: EOD today. I'll tag relevant owners.

lex (customer-sre): tagging for follow-up: @support-leads for outreach checklist.

emily (prod-analytics): dumping final artifact links into incident ticket: logs, hit-rate charts, timeline CSV.

maya (SRE): End thread.
